name: drug response overview
title: Prescribing for this patient: after the WHO steps, verify the standard treatment suits them; age at both ends of life, kidney and liver disease, other drugs and food, and genes, race and sex each change how much drug reaches the target or how it responds, and each column gives what changes and what to do

root.title: Prescribing for THIS patient: what changes the DRUG or the DOSE?
lines: World Health Organization (WHO) steps: 1 define the problem → 2 the goal, WITH the patient → 3a the standard treatment (number needed to treat low, to harm high) → 3b VERIFY it suits them → 4 start → 5 inform + warn → 6 monitor, stop
verify: every other medication + supplement · allergies (what happened?) · past history · cost, access · does the patient AGREE?

groups.title: AGE: both ends of life
lines: healthy adults: usually the standard dose

groups.title: ELIMINATION: kidney or liver disease?
lines: may need a dose change + monitoring

groups.title: What ELSE changes the response?
lines: the same dose, a different effect

head: h
Child
few child-sized formulations
why: • liver enzymes: past adult by 3–6 years

head: h
Older adult
polypharmacy: 5–10+ medications
act: Review at least YEARLY + at every transition
• am I treating another drug's effect?
• can one drug treat two conditions?

head: h
Kidney disease
glomerular filtration rate (GFR) falls
why: adjust by CREATININE CLEARANCE, e.g. penicillin:

head: h
Liver disease
severity: Child-Turcotte-Pugh
act: Dosing is IMPRECISE: guide it by RESPONSE

head: h
Other drugs · food
risk: polypharmacy, several prescribers, narrow window
why: • rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, St John's wort
act: • angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor + potassium-sparing diuretic → hyperkalemia
• monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI) + cheese or cold medicine → hypertension

head: h
Genes · race · sex
act: • ACE inhibitor alone: less effective in Black patients
• more QT prolongation, statin myopathy, ACE-inhibitor cough
